conviction_note: AUM for the half is already public (RNS 13 Oct 2026), the fee rate is guided at 38-40bp and the stock has sold its last two results despite double-digit EPS growth, so the only thing new is H1 net flows, the interim dividend and current-trading colour. The evidence on flows is peer and inference only (Ashmore's record-low redemptions and +$1.1bn net in Jul-Sep 2026; N91's Q2 AUM fell 1.4% against a roughly -2% blended market). That gives a marginal positive lean (p_up 51) on a 5% move, so the scaled number is +0.1 while the findings sum to +0.6. The gap is the reaction-history veto acting on p_up.

already_public.what: AUM at 30 Sep 2026 £181.4bn (30 Jun 2026 £184.0bn; 30 Sep 2025 £152.1bn); interim results date 16 Nov 2026
FY27 average management fee rate guided at 38-40bp (FY26 40.7bp, H2 FY26 40bp); H2 FY26 flows called 'disappointing', with some expected mandates taking longer to fund
FY26 results: adjusted EPS 17.4p, net inflows £2.8bn ex-Sanlam, Sanlam take-on £18.3bn, dividend 13.4p

new_in_release.expect: H1 net flows are the main unknown. The prior half was +£2.4bn organic (H1 FY26 £4.3bn incl. £1.9bn Sanlam UK); peer and AUM-vs-market evidence points to flat-to-positive flows. Slight positive lean.

Adjusted operating profit up roughly 18-22% y/y on average AUM about 29% higher (Sanlam SA included) at a 38-40bp fee rate; adjusted EPS around 9.3p vs 8.4p. Derived from public AUM and the public fee guide, so it is mostly already computable.
Interim DPS likely up from 6.0p. Policy-driven, little surprise expected.
Post-period: EM equities (EEM) -8.5% and gold (GLD) -6.8% from 30 Sep to 12 Nov 2026, so any October AUM or current-trading colour skews soft. Mild negative.
No formal profit guidance; a fee-rate guide update is possible. Unknown.

bar: FY27 consensus EPS 18p (range 17-19p) and revenue £735.8m from 5 analysts, last updated 2026-07-03 (https://stockanalysis.com/quote/lon/N91/forecast/). A single stale aggregator with no H1-specific bar and no flows consensus, so the bar is effectively unsourced for the half and every size is capped small.

findings.finding: Average AUM for H1 FY27 is roughly 29% above H1 FY26 (quarter ends £171.8bn / £184.0bn / £181.4bn against an H1 FY26 average of £139.7bn), so at the guided 38-40bp fee rate management fees come out around £350m against £290.7m. That is about +20% before costs, and the market can already compute it from public releases.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY26 (3 Jun 2026): adjusted EPS +12% with the stock -4.59%. H1 FY26 (17 Nov 2025): adjusted EPS +15% with the stock -2.37%. Earnings growth has been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. Every input (AUM, fee guide) is public, and the consensus FY27 EPS of 18p already implies about 9p for H1. Filed at 0 under the rule that a finding on a pre-released number is worth nothing.

findings.finding: Ashmore, the closest listed EM-specialist peer, reported $1.1bn of net inflows in the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, split evenly between fixed income and equities, with gross redemptions at their lowest in more than 15 years. That is the same quarter as N91's Q2 FY27, for which N91 discloses AUM but not flows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Flows are the line N91 trades on: FY26 fell 4.59% when H2 flows disappointed despite EPS +12% (https://www.proactiveinvestors.co.uk/companies/news/1093360/ninety-one-shares-swing-sharply-as-solid-full-year-results-fail-to-satisfy-on-flows-1093360.html, title only, 403); Jun 2025 +9.49% on a flow turn.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Ashmore's statement is a month old and N91 has drifted around 203-208p since then without re-rating. The transmission from peer to company is a hypothesis. N91 is half African by AUM, and its weak spot is SA multi-asset, which Ashmore does not run. Sized as a proxy.
findings.independence: Finding 3 (N91's own Q2 AUM against the market series) points the same way from a different source.

findings.finding: N91's Q2 FY27 AUM fell 1.4% (£184.0bn to £181.4bn) in a quarter where its mix of markets fell roughly 2%: EM equity (EEM) -2.4%, world equity (URTH) +1.8%, EM debt (EMB) -5.8%, global bonds (AGG) -4.5%, JSE All Share -1.6%, ZAR -0.4% vs GBP. That points to flat-to-slightly-positive net flows rather than outflows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As finding 2: flows decided the June 2026 (-4.59%) and June 2025 (+9.49%) reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference that sell-side can also make, and the asset-class weights are approximate (FY26 mix: equities 45%, FI 25%, multi-asset 16%, SA platform 10%). Market series from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/EEM?range=1y&interval=1d and the same endpoint for URTH, EMB, AGG, ^J203.JO and GBPZAR=X, read 2026-11-13. The Q1 equivalent could not be made consistent (EZA and J203 disagree by about 7 points), so only Q2 is used.
findings.independence: Ashmore Q1 FY27 flows (finding 2), a different source.

findings.finding: Forty Two Point Two, the staff ownership vehicle associated with CEO du Toit and FD McFarland, bought shares repeatedly through the half-year close: 2,234,202 Ninety One Ltd shares at R45.34 on 28 Aug, and London purchases on 1, 3, 9, 10 and 14-16 Sep, 248,845 shares on 18 Sep, and more on 24-25 and 28-30 Sep 2026 at about 209p, stopping at the period end.
findings.why_not_priced: Each purchase is a public RNS, but the market treats them as routine staff-ownership accumulation, and the stock is unchanged since. The signal is that insiders kept buying at about 209p up to the last day before the close period on a half they could see. Weak, because the vehicle buys routinely and also made an in-specie distribution of 7.18m shares on 3 Aug 2026 (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/ninety-one--n91/tr-1-notification-pdmr-shareholding/9707000).
findings.independence: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/ninety-one--n91/director-pdmr-shareholding/9782640 (18 Sep), https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/ninety-one--n91/director-pdmr-shareholding/9749993 (28 Aug JSE). Same filer, so not independent in substance.

findings.finding: Since the 30 Sep period end, EM equities (EEM) are down 8.5% and gold (GLD) 6.8% to 12 Nov 2026, both core N91 exposures (global EM equity, natural resources, gold). Any current-trading or October AUM figure in the release is therefore likely below £181.4bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed instance of N91 giving post-period AUM in an interim release; Nov 2025 commentary was qualitative.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: market moves are public, though the stock has held flat at about 203-208p through the EM decline, so it has not marked the post-period AUM down. The finding is the residual chance that management quantifies a lower run-rate.
findings.independence: GLD series on the same endpoint (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/GLD?range=1y&interval=1d)

Otherwise nothing the English sources did not already carry: SA domestic press returned nothing dated in the window
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the H1 earnings finding, derived from pre-released AUM and the guided fee rate, went from +0.2 to 0.0

'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series' and 'a proxy is a hypothesis': the Ashmore peer finding went from +0.6 to +0.5, the AUM-vs-market inference from +0.3 to +0.2, the staff-vehicle buying from +0.3 to +0.2, and the post-period market decline from -0.4 to -0.3 (visible to everyone)
'You were right about the number and too small about the move': abs_move_pct went from 4.5 to 5.0, because flows and earnings are new in this release even though AUM is not

'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction': the reaction history (beats sold in Jun 2026 and Nov 2025) moved p_up from 52 to 51, not abs_move_pct; print_vs_bar_pct went from +1 to +2 after computing H1 EPS of about 9.3p against the implied 9p
